doc.title: Tom Porrello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 6, 2023

title: Dinner party of lead trumpeters; mouthpieces and horns
summary: He names Audino, Findley, Triscari and Danny Falcone, and talks about his two mouthpieces and Benge-to-Bach horn change.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Growl, plunger and derby: the trumpet mute tradition

blocks.x: Okay, last question. In the Sunday New York Times magazine they always interview an author who’s just put out some new book and they ask them all the same question: If you could arrange a dinner party of authors both living and not living, who would you invite? So my question to you is if you could do such a thing with lead trumpet players, to have a dinner party, who would be your short list of guests?

Chuck Findley. Ray Triscari. You know those are guys that are all gone now but they were heavy, heavy duty players man. Today some of the guys in Tower of Power, they play really well. You know there’s — we have a band here in Vegas called — what the hell’s the name of it — Jerry Lopez has got a band and it’s Fat City Horns. And they are kicking. But that’s an incredible band. And the lead trumpet player in that is Danny Falcone who was a student of mine, and his father was the conductor for Sinatra for a lot
of years. And Danny’s playing lead on that and he’s playing incredibly well. So he would definitely be invited too.
Do you think you guys would talk shop like okay what mouthpiece are you playing now?

Oh that goes on all the time. My wife always breaks up if anybody comes over the house and says, “You guys can talk about trumpets and mouthpieces for like three days without stopping.” But I’ll tell you something funny about me. I’m not much of a changer like a lot of them are. Some guys have over 100 mouthpieces. I played a Bach 10-3/4 CW when I was a kid in high school and all that. And when I moved to LA I switched to a Bob Reeves mouthpiece. But he copied it except for the backbore, he copied if off of that mouthpiece. So the Bob Reeves, I still play that one. So I’ve had like two mouthpieces since the time I was a kid. You know if it works don’t mess with it. You know?

Yeah. And the horns, they make so many good ones now. I did most of my career on a Benge trumpet and then I switched over about twenty years ago to a Bach sterling silver, which the whole bell section is sterling silver. So for me, that horn like really projects. It projects, it’s got a good fat sound and I do most of my work on that now.
But I’m sure I left out a lot of great trumpet players that I’d invite, but off the top of my head quick I can’t —
Well I would call Snooky Young and tell him about the party so he could go too.

He definitely would be there. That’s for sure. Yeah definitely. We have Tom Delibero, he’s a local trumpet player here, he’s a great player too. He definitely be sure — yeah there are so many good ones you know. Chase used to live here.
